name: PACCAR
description: PACCAR builds heavy and medium-duty trucks sold under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates, and designs its own diesel engines. It earns money three ways: selling trucks through independent dealers, selling aftermarket parts (TRP stores and dealers) for trucks already on the road, and financing and leasing those trucks through PACCAR Financial Services. In FY2025 Parts earned $1,668.0M of pre-tax income on $6.87B of sales versus $870.8M on $19.4B for Truck, so the parts business earns far more per dollar and is steadier through the truck cycle.

businessLines.name: Truck
businessLines.how: One-time sale of a new truck (ordered to customer spec, through independent dealers) at a price per unit; cyclical with freight demand and capital availability. 2025 deliveries fell in all major markets and tariff costs weighed on margin.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment income before income taxes

businessLines.name: Parts
businessLines.how: Aftermarket truck parts sold to over 2,000 Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF dealers and more than 350 TRP stores in 99 countries from 21 parts distribution centers; repeat purchases by the installed base of trucks.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment income before income taxes

businessLines.name: Financial Services
businessLines.how: Interest and lease income on retail loans and leases to truck buyers and on dealer floor-plan inventory loans, funded with commercial paper and term notes; 3-5 year contracts.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), segment income before income taxes

brands.name: DAF
brands.note: European truck nameplate; 13.5% of European heavy-duty, 9.7% of light/medium-duty in 2025

brands.name: TRP
brands.note: Aftermarket parts brand, more than 350 stores
